clue.text: Vera's evasion?

parts.note: Vera is Latin for 'true' in the feminine, so a dodge built from only part of her name's meaning is a statement only partly honest

explanation.walkthrough: Vera looks like a woman's name; in Latin vera means true, and an evasion offers only some of what is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasive statement that is partly accurate but misleading is a common idiom for half-honesty.

clue.text: Spray water over a book

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next

parts.note: to spray water on something is to hose it

explanation.surface: Someone splashes water across a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: To get into Yahoo, help arranged

parts.note: a yahoo is a boorish oaf, a lout

explanation.surface: Helping a boor get organised.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoo looks like the website; here it is the brute from Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means arranged or set out in order, as a page or a garden is.

clue.text: Almost placid North Sea rippling ——- it has a bobble

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop short of the final letter of the word

parts.note: placid means tame

indicators.note: rippling suggests the words North Sea being stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A calm North Sea with waves, and something bobbing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims TAME to TAM; 'rippling' rearranges NORTHSEA into OSHANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish woollen bonnet traditionally has a pompom, or bobble, on its crown.

clue.text: Remove jumper and put off going outside

indicators.note: one piece going outside another surrounds it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram, and 'going outside' wraps it round the jumper. Jumper is not the sweater but the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull out by the roots, hence to remove entirely.

clue.text: To like the Venus de Milo is hard? It's not ugly

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Is it hard to admire the Venus de Milo? She is hardly ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ugly here means threatening, as in an ugly mood, so not ugly means inoffensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean menacing or dangerous, so something not ugly is innocuous.

clue.text: Comes to life in holiday up north

definitions.meaning: rouses from sleep, stirs into action
the annual ... weeks were works holidays in northern English mill towns

explanation.definitionFit: Wakes means rouses; Wakes Week was a traditional factory holiday in Lancashire and Yorkshire.

clue.text: Delay cancelling a clever speaker

parts.note: to delay is to wait

explanation.surface: Postponing a smart talker.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a person known for clever, amusing remarks.

clue.text: Fortune can be very funny

explanation.definitionFit: Making a killing is winning a fortune; a killing joke is extremely amusing.

clue.text: Moving nimbly to get extra sentence overturned properly

explanation.walkthrough: Extra sentence suggests more prison time; it is a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and quick in movement.

clue.text: Bubble quietly, keeping hot, and glow

clue.text: From area, turn back

clue.text: No all-rounder, race covered in fine sweat

clue.text: Trick is dishonest, not initially attracting criticism
